text.p: The European Commission approved on Wednesday Ciba Geigy AG's application for market release of gene modified maize, European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler told Reuters.
"It's approved with some labelling conditions," Fischler said.
The approval followed advice from three sets of EU scientists that there were no reasons to reject the maize, officials said.

Fischler had indicated on Tuesday that the approval would go through. "There's not much alternative than to follow the scientific advice," he told Reuters after a two-day meeting of EU farm ministers ending. The ministers did not discuss the issue.

Approval was likely to ease trade tension between the 15-country EU and the United States, whose farmers have faced difficulties exporting to the bloc after growing their first crops containing the U.S.-cleared, gene-modified maize in this year's harvest.

The maize (corn) was developed by the Swiss chemical company to resist the herbicide glufosinate, commonly marketed as Basta, and to carry the Bt-toxin against corn-borer pests. The maize also carries an antibiotic "marker gene". -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
